name: An app
title: A page, *and nothing declared twice*
lede: Add a Nuxt app in apps/nuxt with the @fougere/nuxt module, and write a page. It names the blog's address and calls it; the fronds run inside Nuxt.
fig: The page names post and an operation. Its rows, its form and its refusals are read from what you already wrote.

grows.label: useQuery(post, 'list')
grows.detail: the posts, typed as Post — no row shape written

grows.label: useFormFor(Post)
grows.detail: the fields, their rules, an error under each — status is left out, it is readOnly

grows.label: publish.error
grows.detail: typed NOT_FOUND | CONFLICT — what publish can refuse, read from its code

grows.label: the fronds inside Nuxt
grows.detail: the module boots them and serves /api and /_fougere/call on :3000

try.command: cd apps/nuxt && npm run dev   # then open localhost:3000/posts
try.output: a form with one field, title — and the posts, each with Publish

whatIf: you publish twice from two tabs? The second click shows Already published, the CONFLICT the handler throws.
